title: Ching Shih (Zheng Yi Sao)
summary: A former Cantonese prostitute, Ching Shih married the pirate Zheng Yi in 1801. After he died in November 1807 she took command of the Red Flag Fleet and defeated fleets sent against her. In 1810 an imperial amnesty was negotiated with the Guangzhou governor-general; she and most of her men were pardoned and kept their treasure.

uncertainty.note: Fleet sizes and the pardon date vary by source; only The World of Chinese gives 1810.

where.modern_name: Guangzhou, Guangdong, China (pinned to the city of her marriage and the 1810 negotiation; her fleet operated along the Guangdong coast)

importance.justification: Led a large pirate confederation off southern China and negotiated an amnesty with the Qing authorities.

sources.title: Meet the Chinese Woman Who Became History's Greatest Pirate
sources.author: Joe Doran

reviewer_note: Sources conflict on fleet size (not stated). World History Encyclopedia gives no 1810 date, only a pardon after about three more years. Pin is a city centroid with 100 km uncertainty because operations were spread along the coast. No related atlas record found.
